settings.heading: How a tissue-culture plant is made
settings.text: Tissue culture is propagation in a laboratory instead of a greenhouse. It is how most of the rare aroids in the world are multiplied today, and it is why they can be sold at a fraction of what a cutting of the same plant once cost.

settings.title: A few cells from a parent plant
settings.text: A tiny piece of a healthy parent plant is taken and sterilised, so nothing comes with it — no pests, no disease, no soil.

settings.title: Grown in a sealed vessel
settings.text: It grows on a nutrient gel inside a sealed, sterile container, in constant warmth at close to 100% humidity.

settings.title: Multiplied, true to type
settings.text: In those conditions it multiplies into many small, identical plantlets — each one genetically the same as the parent, which matters for variegated and collector forms.

settings.title: Rooted, then on its way to us
settings.text: The plantlets are rooted in the lab and shipped to us in sealed, labelled containers. They have never seen a greenhouse, a pest or open air — that is exactly why they need a gentle introduction to your home, which we cover below.

settings.heading: Pre-order or ready to ship
settings.text: Most plants on the site are offered at two stages, and the stage is the option you pick on the product page. Same plant, different point in its journey.

settings.title: Pre-order
settings.text: Reserved from our next laboratory batch. Each batch has a cut-off date; after it closes we place the order with the lab, the plants arrive in Canada, are inspected, and ship to you — usually two to three weeks after the cut-off. Your price is locked the moment you order.

settings.title: Ready to ship
settings.text: Already here, rooted and acclimated by us. These have been through the settling-in period and are the quickest way to a plant on your shelf.

settings.title: Mature specimens
settings.text: A small number of established, larger plants — grown on well past the plantlet stage. Each listing is a single plant, photographed as it is.

settings.text: Pre-ordering early gets the best batch pricing and a place at the front of the queue — plants are allocated in the order pre-orders are placed. Here is what happens after you order.

settings.text: The batch closes on its cut-off date and we place the order with our laboratory partners. Orders after the cut-off go into the next batch.

settings.heading: What arrives, and how to settle it in
settings.text:
A tissue-culture plantlet arrives small, in the sealed container it left the lab in, with roots but no soil. It has lived its whole life at near 100% humidity, so the first few weeks are about bringing it gently down to the humidity of a normal room. That process is called acclimation, and it is the one thing that decides how a plantlet does.

Photograph it the day it arrives, then follow the five stages below. The full step-by-step guide and the free starter kit are underneath.

settings.title: Tissue-culture starter kit

settings.heading: Every plant is covered for 30 days
settings.text:
Young plants carry risk, and we think it should sit with us. If a plant you bought doesn’t pull through within 30 days of delivery, we replace it — free on plants under $200, and at 50% of what you paid on plants $200 and over. You cover a flat $14.99 replacement shipping. One condition we can’t waive: a photo of the plant the day it arrives, before you unpack it.

If a plant arrives dead or badly damaged, that is a different, better route: contact us within 24 hours of delivery and it can end in a full refund.

settings.heading: Shipping, simply
settings.text: We ship within Canada only, with tracking emailed the moment a parcel leaves. We don’t ship to P.O. boxes, and in extreme weather we may hold a parcel back a few days — a plant that arrives late beats one that arrives frozen.

settings.heading: The honest small print
settings.text: A few things that are true of every live plant, and of tissue culture in particular.

settings.question: Will my plant look like the photo?
settings.answer: Each plant is its own plant. Size, leaf count and variegation vary naturally, and product photos are representative examples. Plantlets arrive small — that is the point of the price.

settings.question: Is variegation guaranteed?
settings.answer: Tissue culture keeps the genetics of the parent, but variegation is a living pattern that changes with growing conditions and over time. Future patterns can’t be guaranteed unless a listing says so.

settings.question: A leaf is yellow or bent after shipping. Is something wrong?
settings.answer: Usually not. Some yellowing, a bent leaf or a little melt on older leaves is normal shipping and acclimation stress, as long as new growth keeps coming. Photograph it on arrival anyway — that photo is what protects you.

settings.question: Are the plants pest-free?
settings.answer: Tissue culture is sterile by nature and we inspect every plant before it ships. We still recommend a short quarantine from your other plants, as you would with any new arrival.

settings.question: Can I cancel a pre-order?
settings.answer: No. Once a batch closes we have already paid the laboratory for your plant, so pre-orders can’t be cancelled. Orders of ready-to-ship plants can be cancelled any time before they ship.

settings.question: Who is AgaPlantz?
settings.answer: A small Canadian plant shop in Brampton, Ontario, built out of a personal collection of rare aroids. We specialise in Philodendron, Alocasia, Monstera, Anthurium and Begonia, most of it grown from tissue culture and acclimated here before it reaches you.
